title: Hard Words
materials: Household rhythm sticks or wooden spoons
quest_mission: Join Nerissa & Ronan in Aquaria on an acoustic sensory quest to explore Hard Words.
rhythm_ignition: Teacher models a steady 2-minute rhythmic call-and-response beat to 'Hard Words', synchronizing clapping and vocal chanting with the children.
tactile_ritual:
The Hands-On Sensory Discovery:
1. Children gather in a circle with tactile items.
2. Follow the musical cues of Hard Words to touch, sort, and move in rhythmic unison.
3. Pair high-reach movements with deep somatic exhalations.
4. Freeze in quiet stillness at the final chord.

socratic_wonder_circle.rhythm_cue: Passing Shell Slow-Syllable Tap (85 BPM: Slow Down -> Notice Feelings -> Break Into Beats)
socratic_wonder_circle.wait_time_rule: Hold a calm 4-beat pause after every question before inviting responses.
prompts: Thoughts Underlying Feelings (S-4): When you hear a big multi-syllable word like 'Louisiana' or 'vegetables', what thought makes your tummy feel frustrated—and what calm thought helps you slow down?
Fairmindedness (S-3): If a friend stumbles over a tricky word in circle time, how does it feel from their side of the rug if others laugh versus if everyone slows down and taps syllables together?
Overcoming Egocentricity (S-2): Why is a word that feels easy for one person sometimes brand-new and hard for someone learning another language or starting out?

age_tier_scaffolds.Sprouts (Ages 2–4): Tap slow syllables on knees ('spa-ghet-ti') and cheer every brave try.
age_tier_scaffolds.Pathfinders (Ages 4–5): Swap spots on the rug to practice encouraging a friend trying a tricky word.
age_tier_scaffolds.Wayfarers (Ages 6–7): Name the hidden thought behind frustration ('I can't do it!') and replace it with a fairminded strategy ('Break it into beats!').

domain_spider.language: Articulate clear auditory phrasing and target vocabulary connected to Hard Words.
domain_spider.cognitive: Identify rhythmic patterns, tempo shifts, and conceptual categories in Aquaria.
domain_spider.physical: Gross motor whole-body balance, bilateral coordination, and fine motor finger rhythm.
domain_spider.science_sensory: Tactile exploration of real-world materials and acoustic auditory pitch discrimination.
domain_spider.social_emotional: Cooperative participation, shared attentional focus, and calming self-regulation.

teacher_whisper: Auditory rhythmic pacing stimulates brainstem regulation and synchronizes attention across the classroom without visual screen fatigue.

standards.kindergarten_readiness: Actively participates in screen-free multi-sensory rhythm rituals and articulates key conceptual observations.
